note: Generated by scripts/collect-cleancode.mjs from the repositories. Do not hand-edit.

gofmt.name: gofmt-clean tree
gofmt.source: the fleet's own gate: `make fmt-check` fails when `gofmt -l .` prints anything
gofmt.checks: Formatting is the cheapest clean-code property: mechanical, total, and already wired into every Makefile and CI run. A file here is a file the gate missed.

funcs.name: Small functions
funcs.characteristic: Functions (Clean Code: functions should be small)
funcs.source: measured: named function length in lines, tests and generated files excluded
funcs.target: <= 2% of named functions longer than 60 lines
funcs.checks: Clean Code’s first rule of functions is that they should be small; the second is that they should be smaller than that. 60 lines is the stated bar; 2% is the stated tolerance, not a fitted one.

nesting.name: Flat control flow
nesting.source: measured: nested if/for/range/switch/select statements; a function literal resets the count
nesting.target: 0 functions with control flow nested deeper than 4
nesting.checks: Every extra nesting level is another thing a reader (and an agent) must hold in memory. Else-if chains count once; the threshold is the classic four.

files.name: Small files
files.source: measured: non-test Go file line counts, generated files excluded
files.checks: Long files mix reasons to change. The fleet’s hexagonal layout gives every file a home; a file past 800 lines has usually outgrown its package.

docs.name: Documented API surface
docs.source: measured: exported funcs, types, vars, consts without a doc comment
docs.target: >= 90% of exported symbols carry a doc comment
docs.checks: Clean Code distrusts comments that repeat the code — but a doc comment on an exported symbol is the contract every other context reads. The fleet’s pinned linter set does not check this; this page is the only place it is counted.

naming.name: Idiomatic names
naming.source: measured: exported identifiers containing underscores (scored); package stutter counted, never scored
naming.checks: MixedCaps, no underscores, is Go’s naming law. The golint stutter rule was evaluated and deliberately not scored: the fleet’s CloudEvents grammar mandates entity-first event names (promise.PromiseMade), which the rule flags by design. Stutter is counted and shown as evidence, not a failure.

debt.name: No debt markers
debt.source: measured: TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX in comments of code files (AST comments in Go; comment-looking lines elsewhere), tests and fixtures excluded
debt.checks: A TODO is a promise to a future reader. In a fleet written with AI agents the honest question is whether debt accumulates at all; the counter answers it for every language, not just Go. Markers inside string literals or map keys are data, not debt, and are not counted.

dup.name: No copy-paste functions
dup.source: measured: identical function bodies (whitespace and comments stripped) of 5+ lines
dup.target: <= 2% of named functions are exact duplicates
dup.checks: Fowler’s most cited smell. Exact duplicates across a repo’s cmd/ binaries and adapters (the same newLogger, the same readiness check) are counted per repository; some structural repetition across separate services is by design — each context is its own repo with no shared fleet library.

lint.name: Lint wired into the pipeline
lint.source: counted: golangci-lint / eslint / terraform fmt / ruff / hadolint / actionlint in Makefiles, configs and CI workflows
lint.target: the repository’s linter runs in CI or pre-commit, not only on a willing machine
lint.checks: A linter that is installed but not wired is a wish. The check reads the Makefile, the lint configs and the workflows and names what it found.

hooks.name: Pre-commit hygiene
hooks.source: counted: lefthook.yml with fmt/vet/lint (or equivalent) jobs
hooks.target: lefthook pre-commit runs the fast gates before a commit exists
hooks.checks: The fleet standard is lefthook wrapping the Makefile sensors, so one definition of each gate runs locally and in CI. A repo without hooks relies on remembering.
